title: How far? The extent of chemical change
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: R2.3#c02 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.3#c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.3#c11 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.3#c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: R2.3#q01, R2.3#q03, R2.3#q04, R2.3#q06, R2.3#q02, R2.3#q17, R2.3#q05, R2.3#q07, R2.3#q16, R2.3#q08, R2.3#q09, R2.3#q10, R2.3#q12, R2.3#q11, R2.3#q13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Closed system
items.clue: No matter can enter or leave, though energy can.

items.label: Position of equilibrium
items.clue: The relative amounts of reactants and products in the mixture.

items.label: Le Châtelier’s principle
items.clue: A balanced mixture shifts so as to oppose a change in conditions.

items.label: Dynamic equilibrium
items.clue: Forward and backward rates are equal and not zero, so amounts stay constant.

questions.stem:
Hydrogen and iodine are heated in a sealed flask at constant temperature until the amount of hydrogen iodide no longer changes:
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)
Which statement must be true of the mixture at this point?

options.text: No HI forms or decomposes now, as both reactions have stopped.
HI forms and decomposes at equal rates, so its amount stays the same.
The concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI have become equal to each other.
Half of the hydrogen and iodine has been converted into hydrogen iodide.

questions.explanation: The system is in dynamic equilibrium: in the closed flask the forward and backward reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI are constant although the reactions have not stopped.

questions.stem:
Which is the equilibrium constant expression for the following reaction?
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)

options.text: K = [N₂][H₂]³/[NH₃]²
K = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³)
K = [NH₃]²/([N₂]+[H₂]³)

questions.explanation: Products over reactants, with each concentration raised to the power of its coefficient in the equation: [NH₃]² on top, [N₂] and [H₂]³ multiplied together on the bottom.

questions.stem:
At a certain high temperature, K = 3.16 × 10⁻¹⁰ for the reaction
2H₂O(g) ⇌ 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)
What is the value of K for the following reaction at the same temperature?
2H₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2H₂O(g)
questions.explanation: The second reaction is the reverse of the first, so K = 1/(3.16 × 10⁻¹⁰) = (1/3.16) × 10¹⁰ = 0.316 × 10¹⁰ = 3.16 × 10⁹. The very large value shows that, at this temperature, the formation of water lies far to the right.

questions.stem:
The following system is at equilibrium in a sealed container:
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)
More hydrogen is injected, and the temperature and volume are kept constant. Which statement about the new equilibrium mixture, compared with the original one, is correct?

options.text: K has a larger value than in the original mixture.
[H₂] has returned to exactly its original value.
[I₂] is lower than in the original mixture.
[HI] is the same as in the original mixture.

questions.explanation: The added H₂ causes net forward reaction, which uses up I₂ as well as H₂ and forms HI; the volume is constant, so [I₂] falls. K is unchanged because the temperature is unchanged.

questions.stem: Some liquid bromine is placed in a flask, which is then stoppered and kept at constant temperature. The brown colour of the vapour above the liquid deepens at first and then stays constant. Which statement about the flask once the colour is constant is correct?

options.text: Bromine still evaporates and condenses, and the two processes occur at equal rates.
Bromine has stopped evaporating, because the vapour above the liquid is saturated.
The system cannot be at equilibrium, because no chemical reaction takes place.
The concentration of Br₂ is now the same in the liquid and in the vapour.

questions.stem:
Methanol can be made from carbon dioxide and hydrogen in a homogeneous gas-phase equilibrium:
CO₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g) + H₂O(g)
Which is the equilibrium constant expression for this reaction?

options.text: K = [CH₃OH]/([CO₂][H₂]³)
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂][H₂])
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂]·3[H₂])
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂][H₂]³)

questions.explanation: Correct. All four species are gases in a single phase, so every concentration appears: products over reactants, each raised to the power of its coefficient. 3H₂ gives [H₂]³, and H₂O(g) is a gaseous product whose concentration changes, so [H₂O] stays in the numerator.

questions.stem: For the reaction A(g) ⇌ B(g), K = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ at 298 K. Which statement about this reaction at 298 K is correct?

options.text: At equilibrium, the mixture consists almost entirely of A.
At equilibrium, A and B are present in similar amounts.
The small value of K shows that equilibrium is reached slowly.
Adding a catalyst would increase the equilibrium yield of B.

questions.explanation: K ≪ 1, so [B]/[A] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ at equilibrium: the position of equilibrium lies far to the left and very little A is converted into B.

questions.stem:
The forward reaction in the following equilibrium is exothermic:
2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)
The temperature of the equilibrium mixture is increased at constant pressure. How do the amount of SO₃ and the value of K at the new equilibrium compare with those at the original equilibrium?

options.text: A larger amount of SO₃ and a larger value of K.
A smaller amount of SO₃ and a smaller value of K.
An unchanged amount of SO₃ and an unchanged K.
A smaller amount of SO₃ and the same value of K.

questions.explanation: Raising the temperature favours the endothermic direction, here the backward reaction, so less SO₃ is present at the new equilibrium; K depends on temperature and, for an exothermic forward reaction, decreases.

questions.stem: For the reaction X(g) ⇌ Y(g), K = 1.0 × 10¹⁵ at 298 K. Which statement about this reaction at 298 K is correct?

options.text: At equilibrium, the mixture is made up almost entirely of X.
At equilibrium, almost all of X has been converted into Y.
At equilibrium, X and Y are present in similar amounts.
The large value of K shows that equilibrium is reached quickly.

questions.explanation: K ≫ 1, so [Y]/[X] = 1.0 × 10¹⁵ at equilibrium: the position of equilibrium lies far to the right and the reaction goes almost to completion.

questions.stem:
A gas syringe contains an equilibrium mixture of brown NO₂ and colourless N₂O₄:
2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g)
The intensity of the brown colour depends on [NO₂]. The plunger is pushed in to halve the volume, and the temperature is kept constant. How does the colour of the new equilibrium mixture compare with that of the original mixture?

options.text: Paler, since the shift takes [NO₂] below its first value.
The same, since the shift restores [NO₂] to its first value.
Darker, since no shift can occur while K is unchanged.
Darker, since the shift removes only part of the extra NO₂.

questions.stem:
In a sealed bottle of carbonated water at constant temperature, carbon dioxide gas above the liquid is in equilibrium with dissolved carbon dioxide:
CO₂(g) ⇌ CO₂(aq)
When the cap is removed, gas escapes from the space above the liquid and bubbles of CO₂ form in the liquid. Which statement explains the formation of the bubbles?

options.text: The pressure of CO₂(g) falls, so the equilibrium shifts to the left.
Opening the bottle lowers K, so less CO₂ can stay dissolved.
The equilibrium was static while sealed, and restarts on opening.
CO₂ leaves the liquid until its former gas pressure is restored.

questions.stem:
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)
At one instant, a sealed 2.00 dm³ vessel contains 0.100 mol N₂, 4.00 mol H₂ and 0.200 mol NH₃. What is the value of the reaction quotient, Q, at this instant?

N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)
N₂O₄ is placed in a sealed vessel at an initial concentration of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ and the mixture is allowed to reach equilibrium at constant temperature. At equilibrium, [NO₂] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³. What is the value of K at this temperature?
questions.explanation: Forming 0.080 mol dm⁻³ of NO₂ uses 0.040 mol dm⁻³ of N₂O₄ (1 : 2 ratio), so [N₂O₄]eqm = 0.200 − 0.040 = 0.160 mol dm⁻³. K = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = 0.080²/0.160 = 0.040.

questions.stem:
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)   K = 50 at temperature T
A sealed vessel at temperature T contains H₂, I₂ and HI, each at a concentration of 0.20 mol dm⁻³. Which statement describes what happens as the mixture reaches equilibrium at temperature T?

options.text: There is net backward reaction, and [HI] decreases.
No net reaction occurs, as the concentrations are equal.
There is net forward reaction, and [HI] increases.
K becomes 1.0, and the concentrations stay the same.

questions.explanation: Q = [HI]²/([H₂][I₂]) = 0.20²/(0.20 × 0.20) = 1.0. Q < K, so the ratio of product to reactant terms is too small: net forward reaction increases [HI] and decreases [H₂] and [I₂] until Q = 50.

questions.stem:
N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g)   K = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ at a certain high temperature
A sealed vessel at this temperature initially contains N₂ at 0.80 mol dm⁻³ and O₂ at 0.20 mol dm⁻³, and no NO. What is the concentration of NO at equilibrium?

options.text: 1.6 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³
8.0 × 10⁻⁷ mol dm⁻³
1.3 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³
3.2 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³

questions.explanation: Because K is very small, very little N₂ and O₂ react, so [N₂]eqm ≈ 0.80 and [O₂]eqm ≈ 0.20 mol dm⁻³. Then [NO]² = K[N₂][O₂] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ × 0.80 × 0.20 = 1.6 × 10⁻⁶, so [NO] = 1.3 × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³. Only 6.3 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ of each reactant is used, which confirms the approximation.
